chapter_theme: One song at Kodi, the Kuzhagar temple (கோடி - குழகர் கோயில்): a plea against women, land-greed and wealth-greed, before the body falls into Death's mouth like a frog in a snake's, asking to say 'Murugavel' once among the devotees.

842.reading: The poet asks that he not wander daily in love of women with cloud-dark hair, nor strive like a fish in the waves out of greed for land and wealth, and that before his body falls into Death's tongue like a frog into a snake's mouth he be granted to join those who chant with love and say once 'Muruga Vel'. The praise tells how Murugan sported with the peacock-like Kurava girl guarding millet from her platform and drove the bright vel into the hunters who came searching for a thief, names him son of Uma who plays with the ash-smeared Lord and younger brother of the elephant-faced one, at Kodi of Kuzhagar.
842.nuance: காலனது நா அரவ வாயில் இடு தேரையென: Death's tongue is a snake's mouth and the body a frog already in it, an image of death as already begun. புவியாசை பொருளாசை, the greed for land and for wealth, is named beside the women.

links.note: 842 asks that before his body falls into Death's tongue like a frog into a snake's mouth (காலனது நா அரவ வாயிலிடு தேரையென) he be granted to say once 'Muruga Vel' among devotees. Kural 335 says good deeds must be done at once, before the hiccup comes and stops the tongue (நாச்செற்று விக்குள்மேல் வாராமுன்). Both set a deadline at the tongue; the song's one good deed is a single utterance of the name.
